title: C240B — Audio Control Module (ACM)
introduction:
I read this audio control module connector like a backstage patch bay: microphone signals, audio paths, active-noise-cancellation outputs and a satellite-radio data link meet in the same housing, but their labels give them different jobs. Recognizing that variety makes the assignment table much more useful than treating every wire as another speaker lead.

Begin with the connector identification table, use the drawing to locate a printed cavity label, then find that label in the Cavity column. Read across the whole row to connect its circuit identifier with the color, gauge, function and terminal part number. Preserve the positive and negative designations and the named channel or link; those distinctions are part of the connection’s identity. Repeated cavity entries record alternatives whose applicability is not explained by the blank Qualifier cells.

This reference identifies connections and catalogs the displayed pigtail parts. It does not teach access, physical viewing direction, connector release, probing, testing or pigtail installation. Gauge conventions, metadata codes and the starred color notation remain uninterpreted. The overall pin-count entry conflicts with the illustrated cavity range, so I leave that question open rather than sketching extra connections into the margins.

edits.why: The drawing places cavity labels in vertical columns, with each column increasing downward. Adjacent labels across a row are not consecutive, so I use the printed label rather than count sideways from a convenient corner. Gray-filled positions correspond here to rows without assigned circuits. The large side projection and the smaller housing features help distinguish the drawing’s sides, but they do not establish release movements or the physical viewing direction.

Follow each cavity across its own row. Function labels distinguish ambient-noise microphone connections, active-noise-cancellation outputs, the satellite digital-radio data link and gateway-module audio paths. Match positive and negative entries by their full function descriptions; a negative signal label is not an instruction to connect it to chassis ground. Likewise, a data-link entry is not interchangeable with an audio-channel entry. Some repeated cavity entries differ in color, but no qualifier chooses between them. Keep the starred color and the abbreviated output description literal rather than guessing a shield, drain or additional channel. The Used field records reference data, not whether a circuit has passed an electrical check.

I use this table to distinguish the kit number, service part and engineering shell identifiers; they serve different catalog roles. Keep the recorded gauge, material, cavity count and image filename attached to their original row. The kit listing supports a parts lookup, but it does not establish vehicle-specific suitability or teach splicing, terminal selection or installation.

originalAuthorHold: The identification table gives Pin Count as 28, while the drawing and assignments cover cavities 1–26 and the displayed pigtail row specifies 26 cavities. Confirm the intended connector count without silently changing any table value.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 56 primary units including complete raw-text u56 omitted from the original first CLI chunk coverage, four complete source pages and sole figure, and 3 edits. Public fields unchanged from original author; count and repeated audio color assignment ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
